# Features

panda-ng is PANDA rebuilt on QEMU 11.1.0: the PANDA runtime (callbacks, plugins, record/replay)
in a QEMU plugin and a patch series, driven from Python through pandare2. Whole-system analysis
runs under TCG; KVM runs guests at native speed, and a snapshot can move between the two. The
table lists each feature, how settled it is, and where its tests run; each section below says
how to use it and which tests and engine patches it rests on.

Guest tests are the `tests/*.py` scripts, run with `tests/run.sh` on the debian-13 and
ubuntu-24.04 images (see
[tests/README.md](https://github.com/panda-re/panda-ng/blob/main/tests/README.md)).

| feature | status | accelerators | tested on |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Python API (pandare2)](#python) | supported | TCG | x86_64, aarch64, riscv64 |

<a id="python"></a>
## Python API (pandare2)

Start a guest, run commands on its serial console, revert to snapshots, read and write its
memory and registers, and register callbacks, all from Python. The `Panda` object owns one QEMU
instance; work that drives the guest and waits for it (console commands, snapshot loads) goes in
`@panda.queue_blocking` functions.

**Use it:** `Panda`, `Panda.queue_blocking`, `Panda.run_serial_cmd`, `Panda.revert_sync`, `Panda.virtual_memory_read`, `Panda.virt_to_phys`, `PyPlugin`

**Docs:** [docs/guides/getting-started.md](guides/getting-started.md), [docs/guides/python.md](guides/python.md), [python/core/README.md](https://github.com/panda-re/panda-ng/blob/main/python/core/README.md), [tests/README.md](https://github.com/panda-re/panda-ng/blob/main/tests/README.md)

**Tests:** `tests/smoke.py`, `tests/api.py`, `tests/reset.py`, `tests/teardown.py`

**Engine patches:** 0041 ([series](reference/patches.md))

<a id="callbacks"></a>
## Callbacks

Run code when the guest translates or executes a block or instruction, reads or writes memory
(virtual or physical, before or after), takes an exception, or changes address space. The
[callback reference](reference/callbacks.md) lists every callback and whether it fires in this
engine.

**Limits.** Callbacks need TCG. Some declared callbacks have no call site yet or abort at registration; the
reference says which. A registered memory callback instruments every load or store even while
disabled, and an enabled physical one costs an address lookup per access.

**Use it:** `Panda.enable_callback`, `Panda.disable_callback`, `Panda.disable_tb_chaining`, `Panda.flush_tb`, `panda_register_callback`

**Docs:** [docs/guides/python.md#callbacks](guides/python.md#callbacks), [docs/reference/callbacks.md](reference/callbacks.md)

**Tests:** `tests/callbacks.py`, `tests/blocks.py`, `tests/blocks_bare.py`, `tests/late.py`, `tests/tbpc.py`, `tests/mem.py`, `tests/physmem.py`

**Engine patches:** 0031, 0035, 0042-0044, 0046-0049, 0053-0054, 0058-0059, 0065 ([series](reference/patches.md))

<a id="plugins"></a>
## C and C++ plugins

PANDA plugins are shared libraries loaded with `panda.load_plugin(name, args)`. panda-ng ships 12
(plugins/config.panda); `buildPandaPlugin` in the flake builds your own against the engine's
headers (examples/consumer shows it).

**Use it:** `Panda.load_plugin`, `buildPandaPlugin`, `cskeleton` (plugin), `cppskeleton` (plugin)

**Docs:** [docs/guides/plugins.md](guides/plugins.md), [README.md](https://github.com/panda-re/panda-ng/blob/main/README.md)

**Tests:** `tests/guest.py`


<a id="rust"></a>
## Rust plugins

rust/panda-bindings is bindgen output for every target (crate `panda`, one feature per target);
plugins/rust_skeleton is a starting point.

**Limits.** No test loads a Rust plugin yet; CI only checks that the bindings compile.

**Use it:** `rust_skeleton` (plugin)

**Docs:** [docs/guides/plugins.md#rust-plugins](guides/plugins.md#rust-plugins)

**Tests:** none yet.


<a id="osi"></a>
## Operating system introspection

Processes, threads, modules, memory mappings and files of a Linux guest, from its kernel's
symbols (an ISF file, as the test images carry). Use the osi_linux and osi_isf plugins, or
pandare2's `Cosi` directly from Python.

**Use it:** `osi` (plugin), `osi_linux` (plugin), `osi_isf` (plugin), `Cosi`

**Docs:** [docs/guides/getting-started.md#a-first-analysis](guides/getting-started.md#a-first-analysis), [docs/guides/plugins.md](guides/plugins.md)

**Tests:** `tests/osi_isf.py`, `tests/asidstory.py`, `tests/kpti.py`


<a id="syscalls"></a>
## System calls

Callbacks on every system call entry and return, with decoded arguments (syscalls2), and on new
processes (proc_start_linux).

**Use it:** `syscalls2` (plugin), `proc_start_linux` (plugin)

**Docs:** [docs/guides/plugins.md#using-a-plugin-from-python](guides/plugins.md#using-a-plugin-from-python), [plugins/syscalls2/README.md](https://github.com/panda-re/panda-ng/blob/main/plugins/syscalls2/README.md)

**Tests:** `tests/guest.py`


<a id="hooks"></a>
## Address hooks

Run a callback when the guest reaches an address, optionally only in one address space (the hooks plugin).

**Use it:** `hooks` (plugin)

**Docs:** [docs/guides/python.md#callbacks](guides/python.md#callbacks), [plugins/hooks/README.md](https://github.com/panda-re/panda-ng/blob/main/plugins/hooks/README.md)

**Tests:** `tests/calls.py`, `tests/hookalias.py`


<a id="hypercalls"></a>
## Guest hypercalls

A guest program talks to the analysis through a hypercall instruction on every architecture.
`@panda.hypercall(magic)` handles one in Python; the hypercaller and hypersyscalls plugins
handle them in C.

**Use it:** `Panda.hypercall`, `hypercaller` (plugin), `hypersyscalls` (plugin)

**Docs:** [docs/guides/python.md#callbacks](guides/python.md#callbacks)

**Tests:** `tests/guest.py`, `tests/mem.py`

**Engine patches:** 0001, 0003-0008, 0045 ([series](reference/patches.md))

<a id="record-replay"></a>
## Record and replay

Record a whole-system execution and replay it deterministically, with any callbacks and plugins
attached during the replay. Launch with `-accel tcg,rr-ready=on` (pandare2 does this) so a
recording can start at any point.

**Limits.** TCG, single-threaded. Snapshot loads are refused while recording.

**Use it:** `Panda.record`, `Panda.record_cmd`, `Panda.end_record`, `Panda.run_replay`, `-accel tcg,rr-ready=on`

**Docs:** [docs/guides/record-replay.md](guides/record-replay.md)

**Tests:** `tests/rr.py`, `tests/rrcb.py`, `tests/rrstop.py`, `tests/rrload.py`, `tests/rr_blocks.py`

**Engine patches:** 0025-0028, 0030, 0037-0040, 0050-0052, 0066-0068, 0072-0073 ([series](reference/patches.md))

<a id="snapshots"></a>
## Snapshots

Save the whole VM into its qcow2 image and revert to it (`snap`, `revert_sync`), with an
`after_loadvm` callback after each load. Snapshots load across hosts with different page sizes,
and a savevm right after a loadvm takes as long as any other.

**Use it:** `Panda.snap`, `Panda.revert_sync`, `Panda.delvm`

**Docs:** [docs/guides/snapshots.md](guides/snapshots.md)

**Tests:** `tests/reset.py`, `tests/api.py`

**Engine patches:** 0061, 0063, 0074-0075 ([series](reference/patches.md))

<a id="fast-restore"></a>
## Fast restore

Snapshot RAM and device state in host memory and restore only what changed since, for fuzzing
loops: `panda_fast_snap` and `panda_fast_restore`. Every clock rewinds, the x86 TSC included.
tests/fuzz.py runs a fuzzing loop with it.

**Limits.** TCG only, and not while recording or replaying (both refuse).

**Use it:** `panda_fast_snap`, `panda_fast_restore`, `panda_fast_delete`

**Docs:** [docs/guides/snapshots.md#fast-restore](guides/snapshots.md#fast-restore)

**Tests:** `tests/fastrestore.py`, `tests/fastrestore_guards.py`, `tests/fastrestore_hotplug.py`, `tests/fastrestore_vsock.py`, `tests/fuzz.py`

**Engine patches:** 0055-0057, 0060, 0064, 0076 ([series](reference/patches.md))

<a id="kvm"></a>
## KVM

Run x86_64 and arm64 guests under KVM at native speed, with guest hypercalls and port I/O
reaching the host, hardware breakpoints, and plugin memory accesses that page in what the guest
hasn't touched.

**Limits.** PANDA callbacks, record/replay and fast restore need TCG. No CI runner has KVM yet.

**Use it:** `-accel kvm`, `qemu_plugin_register_vcpu_bp_cb`, `qemu_plugin_hw_breakpoint_insert`

**Docs:** [docs/guides/kvm.md](guides/kvm.md)

**Tests:** `engine/tests/guest/kvm.sh`

**Engine patches:** 0009, 0016, 0023, 0034 ([series](reference/patches.md))

<a id="kvm-tcg"></a>
## Moving a running guest between KVM and TCG

Boot under KVM, snapshot (savevm or migrate to a file), and load the snapshot under TCG to
analyse it, or the other way round; x86_64, and aarch64 with its GIC. The snapshot can move
between hosts, e.g. from an arm64 board running KVM to an x86_64 workstation running TCG.

**Limits.** The CPU model must match on both sides (`-cpu host` under KVM and the same named model under
TCG), and so must the devices: build both engines with the same features or pass the same
`-nic`. No test in this repository covers it yet.

**Use it:** `-accel kvm`, `-accel tcg`

**Docs:** [docs/guides/kvm.md#moving-a-guest-between-kvm-and-tcg](guides/kvm.md#moving-a-guest-between-kvm-and-tcg)

**Tests:** none yet.

**Engine patches:** 0022, 0024, 0074 ([series](reference/patches.md))

<a id="faulting-access"></a>
## Memory access that pages in

Plugin reads and writes of guest virtual memory that fault the page in through the guest kernel
when it isn't mapped yet, singly or batched, on TCG and x86_64 KVM.

**Use it:** `qemu_plugin_read_memory_vaddr_fault`, `qemu_plugin_access_memory_vaddr_fault`

**Tests:** `engine/tests/guest/run.sh`, `engine/tests/guest/kvm.sh`

**Engine patches:** 0013-0017, 0032, 0034 ([series](reference/patches.md))

<a id="engine-hooks"></a>
## Translation-time hooks and register pointers

Call a function when execution reaches an address, decided at translation time (6-26 ns per
hit), and read registers through stable pointers instead of the register API.

**Use it:** `qemu_plugin_register_ptr`

**Tests:** `engine/tests/guest/hktest.sh`

**Engine patches:** 0018, 0020, 0036 ([series](reference/patches.md))

<a id="syscall-trap"></a>
## Syscall trap and host-side introspection

Trap guest system calls in the engine, serve them on the host (penguin's syscall engine), read
process state host-side from the kernel's symbols, and redirect the guest from a syscall entry.

**Use it:** `qemu_plugin_set_pc`

**Tests:** `engine/tests/guest/sctest.sh`, `engine/tests/guest/ositest.sh`, `engine/tests/guest/setpctest.sh`

**Engine patches:** 0019, 0021, 0033 ([series](reference/patches.md))

<a id="penguin"></a>
## Embedding for penguin

What penguin (the firmware rehosting tool) needs from the engine: the engine as shared
libraries, a snapshot ABI with a migratable vhost-user-vsock, and reset-request and QMP command
callbacks.

**Limits.** Tested by penguin's own suites, not here.

**Use it:** `penguin_handle_qmp`

**Tests:** none yet.

**Engine patches:** 0002, 0010-0011, 0029 ([series](reference/patches.md))

<a id="machines"></a>
## Custom machines and modules

Describe a board in Python (`MachineBuilder`) or load one as a panda module (`-module PATH`,
`-M PATH:NAME`); `mkBoard` in the flake builds a module against the engine. Modules are checked
against the engine's target and ABI before they load.

**Use it:** `MachineBuilder`, `mkBoard`, `-module PATH`

**Docs:** [docs/guides/machines.md](guides/machines.md), [tests/README.md](https://github.com/panda-re/panda-ng/blob/main/tests/README.md)

**Tests:** `tests/machine.py`, `tests/machine_sw.py`, `tests/machine_builder.py`, `tests/board.py`, `engine/tests/modules/run.sh`

**Engine patches:** 0069-0071 ([series](reference/patches.md))

<a id="packaging"></a>
## Packages

A Python wheel with the engine and plugins bundled, a Debian package, and the nix flake
(packages, an overlay, and `lib` helpers for building plugins and boards).

**Use it:** `wheel`, `deb`, `dist`

**Docs:** [docs/guides/getting-started.md#get-pandare2](guides/getting-started.md#get-pandare2), [README.md](https://github.com/panda-re/panda-ng/blob/main/README.md)

**Tests:** none yet.


<a id="qemu-fixes"></a>
## QEMU fixes

Fixes to QEMU itself that analyses depend on: a longer kernel command line on MIPS Malta, and
cpu_exec_step_atomic under RCU.

**Tests:** none yet.

**Engine patches:** 0012, 0062 ([series](reference/patches.md))
